name: Darien
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Darien, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Darien, IL: the tree lighting at the Old Lace Schoolhouse, Winter Wonderland at Westwood Park, Santa visits and trains nearby.
lede: Darien lights its city tree each November outside the Old Lace Schoolhouse, a one-room school built in 1925, and the Darien Park District follows in December with Winter Wonderland at Westwood Park.
celebrates: Darien celebrates with its neighbors pitching in. The City of Darien holds its Holiday Celebration and Tree Lighting on the grounds of the Darien Historical Society at 7422 Cass Avenue, at the northwest corner of Cass and 75th Street, and the City has thanked the Darien Lions Club, the Darien Historical Society, the Darien Garden Club and the Indian Prairie Library for helping put it on. Families find Santa, face painting, story time with the library, caroling by junior high students and hot chocolate, and the Darien Lions collect new, unwrapped toys. In December the Darien Park District hosts Winter Wonderland, with lights, cocoa and a candy cane hunt at Westwood Park.
lastyear: For 2025, the City of Darien's flyer planned the Darien Community Holiday Celebration and Tree Lighting for Sunday, November 16, at the Darien Historical Society on Cass Avenue. The schedule was planned with face painting from 1 to 3 pm, Santa arriving at 1:30 pm, a children's story time with the Indian Prairie Public Library at 3 pm, caroling by Lakeview Junior High at 3:30 pm and the tree lighting at 4 pm. The flyer promised free hot dogs and hot chocolate while supplies lasted, and asked families to bring new, unwrapped toys for the Darien Lions Toy Drive.
facts: Darien's tree is lit beside a century-old schoolhouse. The Old Lace School was built in 1925 as a one-room schoolhouse to replace an earlier school that burned, and its main room still has a large original blackboard. It was the first school in District 61. The Darien Historical Society formed in 1974 to save it, received the deed on July 4, 1976, and opened the Old Lace Schoolhouse and Museum on July 5, 1980. In May 2026 the society learned the school had been accepted for the National Register of Historic Places. The City of Darien incorporated in 1969.
trains: Darien families can catch Metra in neighboring Westmont, where the station at 18 West Quincy Street sits on the BNSF Line in fare zone 3, with ticket vending machines and 512 parking spaces. Neighboring Clarendon Hills also has a BNSF stop. In December, Metra runs specially decorated Holiday Trains with holiday characters on the BNSF Line, so check metra.com/holidaytrains for the schedule. For a train ride with Santa, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs a holiday train, and the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin runs Santa's Trolley Express.

faq: When is the Darien tree lighting?

The City of Darien holds its Holiday Celebration and Tree Lighting on a Sunday in mid November on the grounds of the Darien Historical Society, 7422 Cass Avenue. It was set for November 17 in 2024 and planned for November 16 in 2025. Check darien.il.us and the City's Direct Connect newsletter each fall for the year's date and schedule.
What happens at the Darien tree lighting?

Recent schedules have included face painting, Santa's arrival, a children's story time with the Indian Prairie Public Library, caroling by Lakeview and Eisenhower junior high students, and the tree lighting itself. The City has offered free hot dogs and hot chocolate while supplies last, and the Darien Lions Club collects new, unwrapped toys for its toy drive.
Where can kids see Santa in Darien?

Santa arrives at the City's tree lighting at the Darien Historical Society each November. In December, the Darien Park District's Winter Wonderland at Westwood Park promises a special visitor from the North Pole, and The Little Gym of Darien on 75th Street has hosted Santa and Mrs. Claus for family photos, crafts and treats.
What is the Old Lace Schoolhouse?

It is a one-room schoolhouse built in 1925 at Cass Avenue and 75th Street, the first school in District 61. The Darien Historical Society restored it and opened it as the Old Lace Schoolhouse and Museum in 1980. It is open the first and third Sunday of every month from 1 to 3 pm, and admission is free.
How can families give back in Darien at Christmas?

The Darien Lions Club collects new, unwrapped toys at Darien City Hall and at the tree lighting. The Darien Woman's Club runs an annual Holiday Soap and Paper Goods Drive, collecting laundry and dish soap, paper towels, toilet paper and cleaning supplies for local food pantries and a local shelter.
